- "6 kg up to 15 kg"
- "15 kg up to and including 50 kg"

Hmm, these are capacity ranges for variants. Let me look at the table structure:

```
Maximum capacity (Emax) | 3 kg up to 15 kg | 6 kg up to 15 kg | 15 kg up to and including 50 kg
Minimum dead load | 0 kg (all)
Accuracy Class | C
Rated Output | 2,0 mV/V
Maximum number of load cell intervals (n) | 3000 | 6000 (colspan 2)
Ratio Y = Emax/Vmin | 15000 | 10000 | 15000
Ratio Z = Emax/(2*DR) | 3000 | 6000 (colspan 2)
Input impedance | 425 Ω ± 25 Ω
Temperature range | -10 °C / +40 °C
Fraction pLC | 0,7
Humidity Class | CH
Safe overload | 150 % of Emax
Output impedance | 350 Ω ± 5 Ω
Recommended excitation | 12 V AC / DC
Excitation maximum | 20 V AC / DC
Transducer material | Aluminum alloy
Atmospheric protection | Silicon resin coating
```

So there are three capacity variants/columns. Column 1: Emax 3–15 kg, n=3000, Y=15000, Z=3000. Column 2: Emax 6–15 kg, n=6000, Y=10000, Z=6000. Column 3: Emax 15–50 kg, n=6000, Y=15000, Z=6000.

So model variants can be defined by the three columns:
- Model 1: Emax range 3–15 kg (n=3000, Y=15000, Z=3000)
- Model 2: Emax range 6–15 kg (n=6000, Y=10000, Z=6000)
- Model 3: Emax 15–50 kg (n=6000, Y=15000, Z=6000)

Model ids could be like "3–15 kg", "6–15 kg", "15–50 kg". Let me use:
- "Emax=3-15kg"
- "Emax=6-15kg"
- "Emax=15-50kg"

The schema's structured value shape only has value/unit/footnote. I could record value as string "425 ± 25"? Rule says numbers not strings. But ± tolerance... I could add a separate characteristic input_impedance_tolerance: 25 Ω. Or represent value as {"min": 400, "max": 450}. Hmm, 425 ± 25 → min 400, max 450. That's a reasonable representation of a range. But it's a nominal with tolerance, not a range. I think {min:400, max:450} is reasonable, or keep value 425 with tolerance. The schema is strict: value must be number | {min,max} | string. I'll use {min: 400, max: 450} for input impedance with unit Ω. Actually maybe better: value: 425, unit_symbol: "Ω", and add separate characteristic input_impedance_tolerance: 25 Ω. That preserves nominal. Hmm. Both defensible. I'll do value 425 and a tolerance characteristic. Actually, to be safe and lossless, I'll do:
  - input_impedance: {value: 425, unit_symbol: "Ω"}
  - input_impedance_tolerance: {value: 25, unit_symbol: "Ω"}
  - output_impedance: {value: 350, unit_symbol: "Ω"}
  - output_impedance_tolerance: {value: 5, unit_symbol: "Ω"}

- temperature_range: {min: -10, max: 40}, unit_symbol: "°C"
- apportionment_factor_plc: 0.7 (0,7 → 0.7)
- humidity_class: "CH"
- safe_overload: 150, unit "%", plus safe_overload_reference: "Emax". The rule example says "150% of Emax → value: 150, unit_symbol: "%" and a SEPARATE characteristic safe_overload_reference: {value: "Emax"} (or omit if too noisy). I'll include it.
- recommended_excitation: 12 V AC / DC → value 12, unit "V", plus maybe power_supply_type... it's excitation voltage type: AC/DC. I could add recommended_excitation_type: "AC/DC". Similarly excitation_maximum: 20 V, type AC/DC. Hmm. Rule 3 example splits voltage/frequency/type for power supply. For excitation, I'll do value 12, unit_symbol "V", and add recommended_excitation_type: "AC/DC". Simpler: keep value 12 V and note type in separate characteristic. I'll add both type characteristics.
- transducer_material: "Aluminum alloy"
- atmospheric_protection: "Silicon resin coating"

Additional text: "The characteristics for nmax, Y and Z can be reduced separately." That's a note; could go into description or footnotes? Not a footnote with marker. I could add to certified_type description. Maybe append. Or add as a matrix description. I'll add to certified_type.description or keep description as given and add a note. The schema doesn't have a notes field. I could include it in description.
